notes.title: Dev Diary #8: The Cards of Who Do Voodoo 🃏
notes.notes: [p]Last time we talked about cards, mana, and crafting. Now let’s look closer at the cards themselves and how they shape the game.[/p][p][/p][p]Every card belongs to a color group:[/p][p]- Blue Cards: Flexible tools for strategy and survival.[/p][p]- Red Cards: Focused on sabotage, traps, and elimination.[/p][p]- Purple Cards: Cards that can turn everything upside down, sometimes helpful, sometimes just silly.[/p][p][/p][p]Here is how they are dealt:[/p][p]- Good Voodoos only draw from the Blue and Purple decks. This way their role always feels consistent and never breaks the immersion.[/p][p]- Bad Voodoos draw from all three decks: Blue, Red, and Purple. This gives them the ability to blend in while secretly having access to sabotage and elimination.[/p][p][/p][p]This setup keeps the mystery alive. At any moment you might see a blue card that looks safe, but there is always the chance that someone is hiding a Red card that can change everything.[/p][p][/p][p]Next time we will dive into Coven and Summonings, the heart of social deduction where discussion and voting can change everything.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45226435/07acb612f1112dde6b055d22f4e16bdb8307f6c1.jpg"][/img][/p][p][/p]

notes.title: Dev Diary 7: Cards, Mana, and Crafting
notes.notes:
[p align="start"]When we first added the card mechanic we faced a tricky problem. Players had to move around the map while also playing cards at the right moments. The pace had to feel just right because you should be able to explore the world and still have time to cast your cards.[/p][p align="start"]To balance this we created our first [b]crafting system[/b]. Crafting not only encourages exploration by sending you around the map to collect items, it also helps keep the number of cards in your hand under control.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45226435/5478c0058bad3653f0f3d8d26d8ba35b513572c0.jpg"][/img][/p][p align="start"]Instead of putting a simple cooldown on card usage we introduced a [b]mana system[/b]. This makes the game feel more immersive since every spell you cast consumes a resource, while also preventing players from spamming powerful cards one after another.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45226435/b0fe2cb893d63e4a89ed98ea6c1e76341d46af9d.jpg"][/img][/p][p align="start"]All of this has been carefully designed and adjusted during development, but the real feedback will come very soon when you get to try it for yourselves in the demo! 

[/p]

notes.title: Dev Diary #6: From 2D to 3D
notes.notes:
[p]When we first started designing the game, our vision was for everything to be fully 2D. The very first map reflected that idea: it was flat, simple, and quite different from the final version you see today. But as we kept working on it, we realized the overall look and feel of the game did not stand out enough from other titles. The world felt familiar rather than unique. Here are an example from the old 2D style and an alternate version of the map. [/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45226435/d051879383aa941e6ae04e1a915be90cc25808c4.jpg"][/img]
To break away from that, we experimented with combining a 3D environment with 2D characters. The result surprised us in a good way. We felt the depth of a 3D world while still keeping the charm of 2D alive through the characters. The new ambiance instantly felt richer and more immersive, and as players ourselves, we looked at it and thought, "This is a place I would want to explore in a game." Below you can see the concept art we drew for the 3D environment alongside an in-game screenshot. Do you like how it turned out? [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45226435/80784ea1df1e8aa0752c150162c337a0e6f43855.jpg"][/img]

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45226435/fda1ba83f3cf8b9ca2036d2e671d64e849f563e8.png"][/img][/p]

notes.title: Dev Diary #5: Designing the Blueprint of The Whisper Castle
notes.notes: [p]When we started working on the map, we looked at how rooms were arranged in old castle blueprints, though we simplified them a lot. We wanted players to feel a natural flow as they walk around while keeping the layout believable. That is why there is a courtyard, the kitchen and pantry are placed to the left of the great hall, and the throne room connects directly to it. [/p][p][/p][p]The Whisper Castle was inspired by the way real medieval castles were organized. Below, you can see the first sketch of the final version of the map. Do you think it feels like a castle you would want to explore?[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45226435/86a0b30ec99bfb9e436520b651c17c58f19645d6.png"][/img][/p]

notes.title: Dev Diary #4: Stitching Life into The Voodoo
notes.notes:
[p]From the very start, the game had a touch of cute but creepy, and the voodoo theme made that feeling even stronger. Once we had settled on the theme and decided that the voodoo doll would represent the player, it was time to figure out what it should look like.[/p][p][/p][p]In [i]Who Do Voodoo[/i], you can be either a Good Voodoo or a Bad Voodoo, but other players do not know which side you are on. That meant our goal was to create a single character design that could represent both sides equally well.[/p][p][/p][p]We kept our [b]cute but creepy[/b] motto in mind throughout the process. We wanted a design that stayed right on that line, something a little unsettling yet irresistibly charming.[/p][p][/p][p]With these ideas in mind, we left the office, found a cozy spot in our building’s lobby, and started brainstorming possible character designs together. After dozens of quick sketches, re-draws, and debates, [i]The Voodoo[/i] was born, a slightly chubby, big-headed doll with a delightfully vacant expression that became the face of our game. We are sharing here and on [url="https://discord.gg/ZuXtq98M"]our discord[/url] that some of the earlier concept art so you can see how [i]The Voodoo[/i] evolved from our first sketches to the final design.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45226435/cae4abca9d567f60f4ca7f40de6f822eeeb16d02.jpg"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45226435/94088ccd360c0843ddbd193c8330d16fccbd90ae.jpg"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45226435/626382729393601846303afcb23d55471210032d.jpg"][/img][/p][p]At launch, there will be up to 16 color options and plenty of cosmetics so you can customize your own voodoo doll to match your style.[/p][p]So, what do you think? Does [i]The Voodoo[/i] look more cute or more creepy?[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45226435/7673d7b42d72e7992904203a291dad46690da109.png"][/img][/p]

notes.title: Dev Diary #3: Choosing The Theme
notes.notes: [h1][b]Choosing the Theme[/b] [/h1][p]For us, it was important to make a game we truly enjoyed ourselves. As a team, we all shared a love for medieval settings, and that was the one thing everyone agreed on from the start. But we also felt that medieval on its own wouldn’t be enough. [/p][p][/p][p]We needed to add something more. While thinking about what that could be, we decided to start with the characters. We asked ourselves, how will players represent themselves in the game? [/p][p][/p][p]The first idea that came to mind was cute frogs. Then we thought, maybe cats, because we all love cats. And really, who doesn’t? There could have been cute characters like hedgehogs or little elves. I’m sharing their early concept art drafts drawn, and I’ll be posting them on our [url="https://discord.gg/ZuXtq98M"]discord[/url] and other social media accounts soon as well. [/p][h3][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45226435/53e47dc1f1668a9b19b474fce812bd17788fce69.png"][/img][i]Earlier Concept Arts of Possible Character Ideas[/i][/h3][p]But still, there wasn’t much of a connection between those characters and the idea of magic. We needed something that would link the medieval world with a sense of mystery and the supernatural. [/p][p][/p][p]That’s when the idea of voodoo dolls came up. [/p][p][/p][p]The voodoo doll character had everything we were looking for. The needles added the creepy, dangerous feel we wanted, while the plush, cotton-filled body gave it a soft, almost toy-like charm. It perfectly matched the strange, twisted vibe we were going for. [/p][p][/p][p]With all these ideas in mind, we started experimenting visually to create a unique voodoo doll character. When we saw the result, we all immediately loved it. That’s when we decided on a twisted medieval voodoo setting for the game. [/p][p][/p][p]The story behind how that character was actually drawn is coming in the next dev diary! [/p]

notes.title: Dev Diary #2: How the idea for Who Do Voodoo was born
notes.notes: [p]We wanted to make a multiplayer game, even though we had never made one before, because we believe it offers something special.[/p][p]We believe multiplayer games offer two kinds of experiences. One happens inside the game, through the mechanics, strategy, and gameplay. The other happens outside the game, in the laughs shared with friends, the stories that come out of each match, and the memories that stay with you.[/p][p]When we started discussing ideas, we quickly leaned toward social deduction. These games are chaotic, funny, and full of great moments with friends. Both the in-game experience and the social layer outside the game felt important, and we wanted Who Do Voodoo to embrace both aspects of multiplayer play.[/p][p]But as much as we enjoyed these types of games, we also felt that they lacked a certain depth. We started asking ourselves what it would look like to take that social energy and mix it with more strategy and worldbuilding.[/p][p]During one of our brainstorming sessions, we realized that all of us really love card games. That got us thinking: what if we made a social deduction game where players could attack each other using cards?[/p][p]We all loved the idea right away, because using cards could add so much strategy to the game. Players could react in real time, surprise each other, and come up with clever moves on the spot. That made everything feel more alive and fun.[/p][p]In a way, the game we’re building now is our way of exploring that question.  [/p][p]Have you ever had a game idea that started from a small “what if” question? What was it?[/p]

notes.title: Dev Diary #1: Why Who Do Voodoo is our most personal game yet
notes.notes:
[p]Hi Everyone!

We’re a team of six creatives at Kuixo. For years, we developed mobile games. Now we’re working on Who Do Voodoo, our first PC title and the game that feels the most like us. [/p][p]So why the change? [/p][p]Working in mobile taught us a lot and gave us a strong foundation. Who Do Voodoo was always designed with multi-platform potential in mind, but during development, it started to feel more aligned with a PC experience, at least for now. [/p][p]At Kuixo, we see games as a blend of art and technology. We care about mechanics and innovation, but also about style, emotion, and worldbuilding. We hoped to craft an experience that feels alive and meaningful, something that brings people together, makes them laugh, and turns into shared memories. [/p][p]With Who Do Voodoo, we’re finally creating the kind of experience we’ve always dreamed of. It’s strange, fun, chaotic, and full of heart. Just like us. [/p][p]Thank you for being here and joining us on this journey! [/p][p]What kind of game would you want to create if you had the chance? [/p]

notes.title: Welcome to Our Story: Dev Diaries Start Here
notes.notes:
[p]Hi everyone, We’re really excited to make our first Steam Community post. Before we launch [i]Who Do Voodoo[/i] in Early Access, we want to tell you the full story behind its development. We also want to introduce ourselves as the team at Kuixo who built it with love and chaos.[/p][p]I’m Burcu, one of the co-founders of Kuixo. I’ll be posting from this account.

Through here, I’d love to share how the game has evolved, what decisions we made during development, and why we made them. If you’re curious, we’d be happy to have you in our [url="https://discord.gg/axngxZxm"][u]Discord community[/u][/url] too.[/p][p]Join us if you're into spooky mysteries, magical mayhem, and uncovering the truth behind smiling faces.[/p]
